title: Ned's Little Peg
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — new alternative pronunciations ch as k/sh, ow as oa.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — new alternative pronunciations ch as k/sh, ow as oa.

pages.text: A sock sits on the line.
pages.illustration: A small cloth sock hanging loosely on an outdoor washing line.

pages.text: The wind tugs at the sock.
pages.illustration: The wind blowing the sock sideways on the line, nearly loose.

pages.text: Ned spots a peg on the grass.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling spotting a small wooden peg lying in the grass below the line.

pages.text: Ned gets the peg in his beak.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling picking up the wooden peg carefully with his beak.

pages.text: Ned hops up to reach the line.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling hopping up to stretch toward the washing line.

pages.text: Ned pegs the sock to the line.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling clipping the peg onto the sock and the line together.

pages.text: The sock sits still in the wind.
pages.illustration: The sock now held firmly still on the line, no longer moving in the wind.

pages.text: Ned did that bit all by himself.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling stepping back, looking at the secured sock with pride.

pages.text: It was just a little job.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling standing beside the washing line, calm and content.

pages.text: Ned grins. He is proud of his little job.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling smiling warmly up at the sock now firmly pegged to the line.
